clue.text: Excellent person's kind deed

parts.note: a class is a kind or category
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: Someone excellent is known for a kindly deed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer or person of outstanding quality is informally called this, an idiom for someone superb.

clue.text: Form company in shed

definitions.meaning: to mould or shape, as metal in a mould
the group of actors in a play
to throw off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions, with 'in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to mould, the actors in a production, and to throw off skin.

clue.text: Armed men cause trouble, getting fed up at gambling joint

indicators.note: fed means given something to take in, so one piece goes inside another
trouble suggests disturbance, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue up means read upwards, reversing the word

explanation.surface: Armed men make trouble, fed up at a betting den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges ARMED MEN CAUSE; 'up' turns AT into TA, and 'getting fed' puts it in to make AMUSEMEN TA RCADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall of slot machines and gaming machines is a kind of gambling venue.

clue.text: Consider what wrestling fans want to do

definitions.meaning: to deal with or look into a matter

definitions.text: what wrestling fans want to do
definitions.meaning: fans want to watch a fight, read as two words plus a bout

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to deal with something, and also to watch a wrestling match.

clue.text: Become gloomy, as stupid person going round university

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a clod is a dull, stupid person

explanation.surface: A dim student turns gloomy at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; 'going round' puts U inside CLOD.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to darken or turn overcast, hence to grow gloomy.

clue.text: Tiring task — fetched kindling

parts.note: a fag is British slang for a wearisome chore
got means fetched, as in went and got

explanation.surface: Gathering kindling is a weary chore.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG here is the British informal word for a tedious job.
explanation.definitionFit: A bundle of sticks tied for fuel is an old word for firewood used to start fires.

clue.text: A soft mineral on the beach

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet, so it stands for soft
ore is a mineral

explanation.surface: A soft rock lies on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on land at the shore, rather than at sea, matches being on the beach.

clue.text: Volunteer involved with region pioneering farming techniques

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A volunteer in a region is a pioneer of new farming methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges VOLUNTEER and REGION together; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s spread of high-yield crops and modern methods in developing countries is called this.

clue.text: Its reporters show industry, dealing with a set of questions

parts.note: trade means dealing, buying and selling
an exam paper is a set of questions

explanation.surface: Reporters demonstrate hard work while handling an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'industry' looks like hard work, but it means a business sector; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A journal for a particular business sector has reporters covering that industry.

clue.text: Officers and men died in this town

parts.note: the staff are a body of officers
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Officers and soldiers perished in this town.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFORD is the county town of Staffordshire in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is a town in the English Midlands, the county town of Staffordshire.

clue.text: A use Cabot had at sea for serving vessel?

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The explorer Cabot finds a use at sea for a gravy jug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the nine letters of A USE CABOT; 'had' and 'for' are links. Cabot was an explorer, which makes the sea plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat-shaped jug for gravy or sauce is a dish used at table for serving.

clue.text: Scavenger one spotted laughing fiendishly

definitions.meaning: an African carnivore that feeds largely on carrion
the spotted species of this animal is famous for its cackling cry

explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a carrion eater and the spotted kind is known as the laughing one.

clue.text: Two-way live broadcaster

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: read both ways, so the word for live is also written backwards

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A broadcaster offers a live two-way link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-way' means BE forwards then backwards. The BEEB is the British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC, the national public service broadcaster.

clue.text: In government ministry, the Queen gains respect

indicators.note: the ministry gains, taking the Queen into its middle

parts.note: Defence is a UK government ministry
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch earns respect from a government department.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'In' is only a link; 'gains' is the container signal, the ministry taking in the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing polite submission or regard to someone is a synonym for showing them respect.

clue.text: After striking these matches end in a point

definitions.text: After striking these matches end in a point

parts.words: After striking these matches end in a point
parts.note: reads like lighting matches, but describes football games where both sides scored and each gets a point

explanation.definitionFit: Football results where both sides score equally earn each team a point in the league.

clue.text: Such journalism needs control, say, before publication

indicators.note: say signals a word spoken that sounds like another spelling

parts.note: to check is to control or restrain
a book is a publication

explanation.surface: This sort of journalism needs editorial control before it goes to print.
explanation.walkthrough: CHECK is said aloud to give CHEQUE; 'needs' and 'before' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of journalism pays sources for stories, so the newspaper is defined by its paying power.

clue.text: Concerned with huge novel penned by black artist

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: bl is an abbreviation for black
re means concerning

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dark artist writes about an enormous novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges the clue word to give UGHE; 'penned by' sets that and the 'concerned with' piece inside black. The painter's name is also spelt Bruegel.
explanation.definitionFit: Breughel, also spelt Bruegel, was a family of Flemish painters, so the name is an artist.

clue.text: Excellent mark, for instance, given to answer

parts.note: M abbreviates mark, the old German currency
eg stands for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: An examiner gives a top mark to an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal slang for great or brilliant, used as an exclamation of approval.

clue.text: Pronouncement of judge feeling heartless

indicators.note: heartless means losing the central letter

parts.note: sentience is the capacity for feeling

explanation.surface: A judge feels no compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes out the middle letter, I, of SENTIENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The punishment a judge pronounces in court is a formal ruling of this name.

clue.text: Damsel in distress once?

definitions.meaning: a young woman, as in the biblical figure of that name
an archaic word for grief or sorrow, now mostly seen in ruthless

explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's name from the Bible and an old word for sorrow and pity.

clue.text: Interfering a bit with talk of decoration

indicators.note: talk of signals the word spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a medal is a decoration for bravery or service
some means a bit, a certain amount

explanation.surface: Someone meddles a little while chatting about honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talk of' makes the decoration a sound-alike; 'with' is a link, and the 'a bit' piece comes second in the answer though first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone prone to poke into others' affairs is intrusive, the adjective for constant interfering.

clue.text: Spies seizing overthrown people's pictures

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

indicators.note: in a down clue overthrown means turned upside down, reversing the word

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: Spies grab photographs from deposed people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' turns the people backwards, giving NEM, and 'seizing' puts that inside the spies. In Britain the pictures means the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is a British way of saying going to the movies.

clue.text: Boldness of communist who's rejected call to join party

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for communist is turned round

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
to ring is to call on the phone
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A communist who spurns an invitation to join the party shows boldness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's rejected' reverses RED into DER; 'to join' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroic daring or reckless courage is an old-fashioned term for boldness.

clue.text: Piece ending programme about royal houses

annotationWithheld.clue: Piece ending programme about royal houses

clue.text: Drive through French city down South

indicators.note: down here means lacking or short of, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France

explanation.surface: A motorist drives through a French town in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue lost 'South'; the page prints it. 'down' takes S out of TOURS.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel around a place by car for sightseeing is a sense of the verb tour.

clue.text: Insect's bite caused upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: tang means a sharp bite of flavour

explanation.surface: An insect's bite caused trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caused upset' reverses TANG; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, a kind of insect.

clue.text: Old drama critic making an entrance

parts.note: an gives the article A
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A veteran theatre reviewer arrives on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue had a stray 'a'. James Agate was a famous British drama critic of the Sunday Times; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: James Agate was a leading London theatre critic in the earlier twentieth century, so the name fits.

clue.text: Additional rooms? Roughly sixteen available

indicators.note: roughly suggests a rough arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: on means available, as in on tap

explanation.surface: Extra rooms, about sixteen of them, are up for grabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' rearranges SIXTEEN into EXTENSI, followed by ON.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition built on to a house to give extra living space is this, a building term.

clue.text: Alternate view was given backing

parts.note: to see is to view

indicators.note: backing means sent backwards, so the word was is reversed

explanation.surface: Another opinion was supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given backing' reverses WAS into SAW. 'Alternate' is a verb here: to swing back and forth.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to move up and down or to and fro, a synonym for alternating.

clue.text: Aussie might have such a flat in one

definitions.text: Aussie might have such a flat

parts.note: being home means being in
a unit is one

explanation.surface: An Australian could live in a flat like this one.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australia this is the usual term for a flat in a block.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian English uses this term for a self-contained apartment within a larger building.
